releaseNotes: Gave the graph engine its first real caller. core/session/bootstrap.ts composes the four pieces that each existed with nothing routing them together — install-entrypoints (executable catalog + runtime binding), migrate-v1 (state/PROJECT_STATE.yaml to state/business-state.json plus a control scaffold), reducer adopt (a truthful manifest + audit baseline so the first session's tamper preflight has a real before), and onboard.ts (grants/waivers/budgets through the reducer) — into one idempotent, dry-run-first command, aliased as npm run session:bootstrap and named in SKILL.md's Autopilot Run Contract. Before this, core/session/run.ts answered the repository's own reference business with "couldn't find its control settings".

Accepted pre-existing material as readiness input. Compile's reads-gate-readiness flip had quietly made a fresh business unstartable: the graph's base is an artifact-level knot (orient-scaffold produces the state file that the producers of its own reads read), so the compiled plan had zero ready nodes out of 82 on a clean bootstrap — invisible until a real caller existed. runstate.ts now accepts a binding with no in-run producing attempt when its file actually exists in the workspace, fingerprinted so changed material still invalidates descendants; in-run production still lands unaccepted pending its own verification, and the read-only planner applies the same rule so its report matches a real session.

Closed the fresh-context verification dead end in headless sessions. run.ts now runs a verification sweep at every empty-frontier point: an independent verifier session (fresh worker subprocess for real runs, a deterministic fixture for checks) judges produced-but-unaccepted work under the same producer-never-verifies refusal rules the operator CLI enforces — now shared in core/engine/verification.ts — with every acceptance attested in the hash-chained audit log, and an accepted node re-opens the frontier so downstream work dispatches in the same session. A verifier that cannot run leaves the work honestly parked and says so in the digest; a rejection parks it under its own named blocker with founder-plain copy.

Fixed two engine defects the new end-to-end check caught: the fixture executor's output fingerprint included the attempt id, so every re-run of a stale node re-invalidated the entire downstream graph and sessions never converged; and a staleness reset could carry a conditional node with an unanswered founder scope question straight into dispatch, because applicability reconciliation only re-parked on a verdict change. Scope questions now re-park whenever they are unanswered and ready-eligible.

Added check:engine-e2e, the engine's crash-test dummy, to the audit: against a throwaway copy of the reference business it proves the bootstrap chain, a first fixture-executor session that dispatches real frontier work, founder approvals granted through approve.ts, a verifier-off control session that MUST leave work parked pending verification (the detector proving it detects), and a resumed session whose sweep clears that backlog to zero with audit attestations. New fixture suite verification-sweep covers the acceptance rules, the pre-existing-material rules, verdict parsing, and the re-park guard.
